display: I manage six matatus on the Thika Road route in Nairobi. I'm a family man and a weekend goalkeeper.

signals.text: County fines on my buses have more than doubled since January. I want to know if the tickets are real, and I don't know where to start.
When I paid some tickets on the e-citizen portal, they showed 'no record'. I'd like someone who understands how county ticket systems work to explain it in plain words.
I have a notebook with every fine since January: date, plate, officer's name, amount. I want to turn it into something checkable, like a clean table or a pattern.
One of my older buses has a leaking head gasket and needs a full engine overhaul. A week off the route costs about KES 30,000 in lost takings.
Costs keep rising: fines, repairs, tyres. I'm looking for cheaper, reliable ways to keep six buses on the road.
My mother's roof water tank in Nyeri is cracked and leaking. I need a 5,000-litre tank and fittings arranged before the short rains in December.
I'm worried about cash handling on the buses. Daily takings sometimes come back short and I can't prove why.
School fees for the January term are a big bill. I need to write a payment plan for the school and I'm not sure how.
December is a slow month for matatu income. I'm looking for ways to smooth cash flow across the year.
I'm under some pressure at the SACCO for asking questions about fines. I want advice on how to raise concerns without making enemies.
My knees are sore from diving on concrete pitches. I'd like to hear from other older keepers about how to keep playing.
Evenings are for my family, so I work best with people who can answer by message during the day.

offers.text: I know the Thika Road matatu route in detail: stage timing, SACCO rules, the weekly NTSA check-in and how the traffic really behaves hour by hour.
I run a small fleet: six 33-seater minibuses and eight drivers and conductors on rotation. I can explain how a small transport business works day to day.
I have contacts at two garages in Githurai, a tyre dealer in Ruiru and a mechanic who works nights. I can introduce vehicle owners and operators to them.
I run a simple M-Pesa float system for daily collections. I can show other small operators how it works.
I keep a dated record of every fine, plate number, officer and amount since January. I can share it in the right context as evidence or data for an audit.
I can host or introduce you to matatu crews and owners on the route for interviews, surveys or pilots, as long as it doesn't take buses off the road.
I can play in goal for a weekend football team in Nairobi, and I can talk about local league life.
I know a small tea farming family in Nyeri through my mother. I can introduce people interested in smallholder tea.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm building a tool that checks traffic or county fine tickets against the official records for small transport operators. Could I test it on real tickets?
catchers.can: I can supply my dated notebook of tickets (date, plate, amount, officer) and compare it with what the county system shows. I can also ask other owners on the route.
catchers.confirm: Does your tool check ticket numbers against the Nairobi county system, rather than only tracking fines for the owner?

catchers.hypo: I'm a journalist or researcher looking into a rise in fines on Nairobi matatu routes. Can you describe what you've seen?
catchers.can: I can describe the pattern from my own notebook (January against August) and the 'no record' cases, in plain words. I will not share the names of people who could be harmed.
catchers.confirm: Are you willing to report on the pattern without naming my drivers or putting them at risk?

catchers.hypo: I'm another matatu owner whose fines have gone up a lot this year. Can we compare notes before I pay the next ticket?
catchers.can: I can compare my record with yours and share what I've learned about checking tickets on the portal. We can work out together what to ask the county.
catchers.confirm: Do you operate a matatu or small public service vehicle in the Nairobi area?

catchers.hypo: I'm a plain-language advocate or paralegal who helps small transport owners understand county fines and how to dispute them without paying bribes.
catchers.can: I can bring a real set of tickets and what happened at the portal, and ask my questions in plain language.
catchers.confirm: Can you explain the process in plain language, without legal jargon, and without suggesting a payment under the table?

catchers.hypo: My family has a small farm and a leaking water tank. Do you know a reliable supplier for a 5,000-litre tank and fittings in the Mount Kenya area?
catchers.can: I'm sourcing the same thing for my mother's farm in Nyeri. I can share the quote I get and any supplier I find.
catchers.confirm: Is the farm in the Nyeri or Mount Kenya region, and is the tank around 5,000 litres?

catchers.hypo: I run a mechanic shop and need a steady stream of repair work on 33-seater minibuses. Can you refer me to owners?
catchers.can: I can pass your name to other owners on Thika Road. I'll first ask my own mechanic and the Githurai garages what they think of your work.
catchers.confirm: Do you work on 33-seater minibuses, and can you do the job on a short timeline of about a week?

catchers.hypo: I'm a nurse or community health worker and need cheap reliable transport for a mobile clinic between Nairobi and Thika.
catchers.can: My wife Esther is a nurse at a county health centre. I can ask her to talk with you about the practical side, and I can look at a route and price that suits me.
catchers.confirm: Is the clinic work on or near Thika Road, and could it run on a fixed weekday schedule?

catchers.hypo: I'm building an app or service for small fleet owners to track daily cash from conductors and drivers. Would you try it?
catchers.can: I can try it on my six buses and tell you what a working conductor and owner actually do with cash and M-Pesa each day.
catchers.confirm: Does your product handle daily collections from several drivers and conductors and record them in M-Pesa?

catchers.hypo: I'm a goalkeeper coach or run an amateur football league. Do you want to play or help us train keepers?
catchers.can: I can join a weekend league as a keeper and talk to others about injuries and playing after 35.
catchers.confirm: Are your matches on weekends in the Nairobi area?

catchers.hypo: I help small business owners with school-fee savings or loan plans, especially when income dips at the end of the year. Can we talk?
catchers.can: I can explain how my income moves through the year and what I need to fund two children's school fees, and listen to a plan.
catchers.confirm: Do you work with small business owners whose income rises and falls through the year, rather than salaried workers?

forbids.text: I can't take a bus off its route for more than a week.
Please use plain language with me, with no legal jargon.
Evenings are for my family, so I don't take calls or meetings then.
I won't accuse named people of wrongdoing without evidence.
I won't share my drivers' and conductors' personal details or their private problems.

projects.name: Thika Road county fines audit
projects.text: Check whether the Nairobi county fines on my matatus appear in the official system, and whether the rise from January to August is real. I have a dated notebook of tickets to start from.
roles_needed: person who understands county ticket records
other matatu owners with their own records

projects.name: Water tank for my mother's farm in Nyeri
projects.text: Buy and fit a 5,000-litre tank before the short rains in December, with a budget of about KES 60,000.

policy.t1: When there's a real sign of a fit, I'll share my fines record, my suspicion that some tickets don't match the county system, the rising costs, and my repair and farm plans.
policy.t2: Once I'm fairly sure of the fit and know who you are, I'll talk about the school fee shortage and my tension with the SACCO.
policy.never: Anything about bribes or 'facilitation' payments I may have made, and private details about my drivers, conductors and family.
